metadata.title: Neocloud stock rout has a silver lining: It's staying contained

content.text:
If there is any upside to the ongoing neocloud stock rout led by CoreWeave (CRWV) and Nebius (NBIS), it's that it hasn't spread to the broader stock or credit markets.
"Just as notable is where the stress has not spread," Barclays strategist Venu Krishna pointed out. "Despite the wider concerns around AI capex and financing, the deterioration in credit has remained largely confined to the neo-cloud complex, with CDS spreads for most hyperscalers little changed. Oracle stands out as the main exception, with its five-year CDS widening by 80 basis points, proportionally as large a change as CoreWeave's. This matters: thus far, credit markets appear to be differentiating between the leveraged balance sheets funding the neo-cloud buildout and the much larger platforms financing AI investment from more established businesses with healthier balance sheets."
Recall that a week ago, the rise in yields on CoreWeave's (CRWV) bonds spurred Elon Musk to post "Yikes" on X in response to a post by venture capitalist Chamath Palihapitiya. You never want to see Musk say "yikes" on anything related to CoreWeave — or anything more broadly.
The word helped fuel a rout in CoreWeave and other neocloud stocks, including Nebius.
But it hasn't spread to other tech stocks or sectors in the S&P 500 (^GSPC), Krishna said.
"CoreWeave, Galaxy Digital, and Cipher Digital fell 30%, 31%, and 44%, respectively, from the end of September through October 19, while the S&P 500 rose by 0.5%. Stocks have also responded asymmetrically to credit: widening spreads prompt outsized declines, while tightening provides limited relief, underscoring skepticism around the neo-cloud business model's durability," he said.
The neocloud group hasn't settled down much this week, despite Musk's bullish tone on AI demand during his SpaceX (SPCX) earnings call. In fact, Bernstein CoreWeave bears slashed their price target on the stock on Thursday and maintained an Underperform rating.
They don't expect the stock to hit $0 — hardly comforting amid this type of volatile trading backdrop.
Brian Sozzi is Yahoo Finance's Executive Editor, host of the Sozzi Unleashed morning show and the Power Players with Brian Sozzi podcast, and a member of Yahoo Finance's editorial leadership team.
